purpose: Fluocinonide is used to reduce redness, swelling, itching, and irritation caused by various skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, allergic reactions, and rashes. It helps calm inflamed or irritated skin and makes you feel more comfortable. It is applied directly to the affected area of your skin.
how_it_works: Fluocinonide is a steroid that works by calming down your body's immune response in the skin. Think of it like turning down the volume on the inflammation that is causing your skin to be red, itchy, and swollen. It reduces the chemicals in your skin that trigger irritation and discomfort.
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or itching when first applied. The skin may become dry or develop mild irritation. With long-term use, the skin may thin out, develop stretch marks, or lighten in color at the application site. Acne-like breakouts can sometimes occur.
warnings: Do not use this on your face, groin, or underarms unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not use it longer than directed, because using it too long or on too large an area can allow the steroid to absorb into your body and affect your hormones. Keep it away from your eyes. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area tightly unless instructed. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 2 to 4 times per day, or as directed by your doctor. Use only enough to lightly cover the area — a little goes a long way. Gently rub it in and wash your hands after applying unless your hands are the area being treated.
